Before we knew it, the forest was on us, and the air grew colder and damper.

glosses: Paid for by.

examples.text: The drinks are on me tonight, boys.
The meal is on the house.
I paid for the airfare and meals for my family, but the hotel room was on the company.

glosses: Toward; for; indicating the object of an emotion.

examples.text: Have pity or compassion on him.

glosses: Indicating the person experiencing an emotion, cold, thirst, hunger, etc.

examples.text: I had a terrible thirst on me.
'[…] the hunger is on me to carry my sword in distant places.' Mynyddog bowed his head.

“Christ, the thirst on me.” “Sure, it's serious work, all that talk of independence.” The theater's stained-glass doors had first flung open in 1904, all in the hope of “rewriting the Irish identity,” of using culture in the fight[…]
“I've got the hunger on me, I do.” Riordan snorted. Hardly a man knew hunger as he did. The prison rations at Point Lookout, spare enough, had been a feast compared to the black years in Ireland.[…]

glosses: Indicating a means of subsistence or sustenance.

examples.text: They lived on ten dollars a week.
The dog survived three weeks on rainwater.

1950s, UK Egg Marketing Board advertising slogan.
Go to work on an egg.

glosses: Engaged in or occupied with (an action or activity).

examples.text: He's on his lunch break.
I'm on nights all this week.
on vacation; on holiday; on a mission; on the job; on the fiddle

glosses: Regularly taking (a drug).

examples.text: You've been on these antidepressants far too long.

glosses: Under the influence of (a drug, or something that is causing drug-like effects).

examples.text: He's acting crazy because he's on crack right now.

glosses: In addition to; besides; indicating multiplication or succession in a series.

examples.text: heaps on heaps of food
mischief on mischief; loss on loss

glosses: Indicating dependence or reliance.

examples.text: I depended on them for assistance.
He will promise on certain conditions.

glosses: Serving as a member of.

examples.text: He is on the jury; I am on the committee.

glosses: By virtue of; with the pledge of.

examples.text: He affirmed or promised on his word, or on his honour.

glosses: By virtue of; with the pledge of.
Ellipsis of I swear on: on my life, on God, on everything, etc.
To the account or detriment of; denoting imprecation or invocation, or coming to, falling, or resting upon.

examples.text: On us be all the blame.
A curse on him!
Please don't tell on her and get her in trouble.
He turned on her and has been her enemy ever since.
He went all honest on me, making me listen to his confession.
His blood be on vs, and on our children.

glosses: Against; in opposition to.

examples.text: The fight was three on one, and he never stood a chance.

glosses: According to, from the standpoint of; expressing what must follow, whether accepted or not, if a given premise or system is assumed true.

examples.text: On naturalism, it is therefore difficult to find a ground for ultimate moral hope.

glosses: In a position of being able to pot (a given ball).

examples.text: All the way around the table, off four cushions, and ... and he's on the black!

glosses: Having as identical domain and codomain.

examples.text: a function on #92;mathbb#123;R#125;

glosses: Having Vⁿ as domain and V as codomain, for the specified set V and some integer n.

examples.text: an operator on #92;mathbb#123;Z#125;

glosses: Generated by.

examples.text: the free group on four letters

glosses: Divided by.

examples.text: Twenty on three.

glosses: Of.

examples.text: I never seen 'im, and that's the truth on it.
Be not jealous on me.
Or have we eaten on the insane root / That takes the reason prisoner?

glosses: At the peril of, or for the safety of.

examples.text: Hence on thy life: the captive maid is mine; / Whom not for price or pray'rs I will reſign: [...]

glosses: Without.
In the Japanese language, a pronunciation, or reading, of a kanji character that was originally based on the character's pronunciation in Chinese, contrasted with kun.

examples.text: Most kanji have two kinds of reading, called "on" and "kun".
